blocks.text:
Paraphrase & Reformulation
เป้าหมาย: ถอดความโดยรักษาขอบเขต เหตุ เงื่อนไข และผู้กระทำ

Use the language of paraphrase & reformulation to complete the unit's practical or interpretive task.
Identify and relay the essential information in the two readings without adding unsupported facts.
Respond to the two listening scripts with appropriate clarification and source-sensitive wording.

Reading A
The original sentence reads, 'Some participants reported that the quieter room helped them concentrate during the trial.' A student's paraphrase says, 'Quiet rooms improve everyone's concentration.' Although shorter and more fluent, it changes the population, certainty and evidence type. Some becomes everyone; self-report becomes an established effect; a limited trial becomes a general rule. A better paraphrase keeps those boundaries: 'During the trial, a number of participants said they found it easier to concentrate in the quieter room.' Effective reformulation may change vocabulary and sentence structure substantially while preserving what the source actually commits to.

Read for purpose, then locate the people, events, conditions and limits. Map claim, supporting evidence, alternative explanation and limitation. Compare sources on the same question. Build a proportionate conclusion and address a fair counterargument. Explain why your evidence supports a claim rather than merely repeating it.

Reading B
Second source: The room change was introduced alongside smaller group sizes. The report does not isolate the effect of either change. Any summary linking quietness directly to improved performance should retain this limitation.

Compare the two inputs: what is shared, what is additional, and what is not known? Use only details actually supplied. All characters, organisations, figures and events in these inputs are fictional classroom materials.

reported that
หน้าที่: รักษาชนิดหลักฐาน
Model: Participants reported that it helped.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

หน้าที่: รักษาขอบเขตกลุ่ม
Model: A number of participants found it helpful.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

หน้าที่: ไม่แยกเหตุโดยไม่มีหลักฐาน
Model: The room change was introduced alongside smaller groups.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

Guided practice: cover the word bank, reconstruct five target expressions, and explain their meaning in these particular contexts. Then use two in a new example. The same word may have a different sense elsewhere.

Listening script A — authored script; recorded audio and human audio QC are pending. Reading the transcript is text-based preparation, not evidence of independent listening ability.

A: My version uses different words. Is that enough?
B: No. Check whether you changed who, when or how certain the claim is.
A: I changed some to everyone.
B: That expands the claim. Restore the original scope before polishing the style.

Listening script B
Use a fidelity checklist: population, time, degree, agency, conditions and evidence type. Compare your paraphrase with the source after drafting. If your reader could draw a stronger conclusion from your version, revise it or clearly label your interpretation.

First pass: identify purpose and main message. Second pass: note essential details and any corrections. Check against the script only after the listening attempt when approved audio becomes available. For now, practise with a teacher or partner reading the script.

Pronunciation and prosody
Use prominence to distinguish your position from a reported view. Pause at changes of argument. Signal concession and contrast with phrasing, without relying on exaggerated stress to make weak evidence sound stronger.

Interaction rehearsal: take both roles. Ask one clarification question, answer it using the source, and check that the other person has understood. Do not equate quietness, accent or hesitation with lack of ability.

Unit transfer task
ถอดความโดยรักษาขอบเขต เหตุ เงื่อนไข และผู้กระทำ

Prepare a 180–240-word response and a 120–180-second spoken response using the unit inputs. Develop sustained positions, evaluate competing practical options and relay complex information with clear qualification.

Planning sequence
1. Identify audience and purpose.
2. Select source details that the audience needs.
3. Mark any uncertainty, unconfirmed arrangement or missing information.
4. Choose two language features from Lesson 2.
5. Produce the response, then check meaning before surface accuracy.

Mediation: explain the essential information to a Thai-speaking classmate who has not read the sources. Preserve dates, quantities, conditions, agency and uncertainty. Say what cannot be concluded.

Online interaction: respond to a request for clarification, then add a follow-up checking question. Acknowledge corrections and revise your message where needed.

Quick review
reported that: Participants reported that it helped.
some / a number of: A number of participants found it helpful.
introduced alongside: The room change was introduced alongside smaller groups.

inputs.label: Reading A
inputs.text: The original sentence reads, 'Some participants reported that the quieter room helped them concentrate during the trial.' A student's paraphrase says, 'Quiet rooms improve everyone's concentration.' Although shorter and more fluent, it changes the population, certainty and evidence type. Some becomes everyone; self-report becomes an established effect; a limited trial becomes a general rule. A better paraphrase keeps those boundaries: 'During the trial, a number of participants said they found it easier to concentrate in the quieter room.' Effective reformulation may change vocabulary and sentence structure substantially while preserving what the source actually commits to.

inputs.label: Reading B
inputs.text: Second source: The room change was introduced alongside smaller group sizes. The report does not isolate the effect of either change. Any summary linking quietness directly to improved performance should retain this limitation.

inputs.label: Listening script A
inputs.text:
A: My version uses different words. Is that enough?
B: No. Check whether you changed who, when or how certain the claim is.
A: I changed some to everyone.
B: That expands the claim. Restore the original scope before polishing the style.

inputs.label: Listening script B
inputs.text: Use a fidelity checklist: population, time, degree, agency, conditions and evidence type. Compare your paraphrase with the source after drafting. If your reader could draw a stronger conclusion from your version, revise it or clearly label your interpretation.

pronunciation: Use prominence to distinguish your position from a reported view. Pause at changes of argument. Signal concession and contrast with phrasing, without relying on exaggerated stress to make weak evidence sound stronger.

rubric.descriptors:
Target B2: Develop sustained positions, evaluate competing practical options and relay complex information with clear qualification.
4 — Fully achieves the specified purpose with precise relevant detail, coherent organisation and effective control at this target level.
3 — Achieves the main purpose; minor omissions or language lapses do not materially distort meaning.
2 — Partially achieves the purpose; important detail, organisation or language needs revision.
1 — Limited assessable evidence; major gaps or distortion impede the task.
0 — No assessable response or wholly unrelated response.
Rate each dimension separately. For mediation, invented facts, erased conditions or reversed agency prevent a high fidelity score. Do not penalise an accent or a defensible alternative phrasing. Scores describe this task only, not certified CEFR attainment.

retrieval.prompt: Without notes: recall 2 target expressions from Paraphrase & Reformulation; explain one source detail and use reported that in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 3 target expressions from Paraphrase & Reformulation; explain one source detail and use some / a number of in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 4 target expressions from Paraphrase & Reformulation; explain one source detail and use introduced alongside in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 5 target expressions from Paraphrase & Reformulation; explain one source detail and use reported that in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.

remediation.action: Return to Readings A/B; underline the evidence for your statement, restore any lost condition, and say explicitly what remains unknown. Retry Q-B2-12-015 and the mediation task.
Revisit the three Lesson 2 models. Identify the intended function, correct the form, and produce a new example. Retrieve the missed expression again after one day.

masteryCheck.decision: Record evidence by construct; no pass mark or CEFR certification without human standard setting.
